title: Why You Need To Freshen Up Your Class Routines
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin identifies the seasonal decline that hits classroom routines as spring approaches, and offers a simple three-step process for reinvigorating them: meaningfully change each routine (combining steps, adjusting pace, or adding challenge), inject an element of fun into the change, and model the new version with visible enthusiasm and precision. He is explicit that the change must offer greater challenge, not less, since the goal is renewed engagement rather than simplification, and that younger students will require more routines and more modeling of the refreshed versions. He frames this as a low-cost, high-leverage seasonal maintenance task, noting it can be rolled out gradually -- one or two routines a week -- rather than all at once, while still delivering a broad energy boost across the whole school day.
points: Freshen up routines by meaningfully changing each one -- combining steps, adjusting pace, or adding a challenge -- rather than merely repeating the original teaching.
Any change to a routine should add a genuine element of fun, like a small silly gesture or movement, to re-engage students emotionally as well as behaviorally.
Model refreshed routines with visible enthusiasm and exacting precision, the same way routines were first taught at the start of the school year.
Refreshed routines can be rolled out gradually, one or two per week, rather than all at once, while still delivering a broad boost in energy and motivation.
quotes: This time of year things tend to get sloppy. Students are feeling the lazy pangs of summer approaching.
Left alone, this feeling will morph into poorer and poorer performance. Only you can do something about it. Because it will never correct itself.
Whichever you decide, be sure that the change offers a greater challenge. This is key.
The best part about changing routines, and the whole purpose of it, is that it transfers to everything you do.
Just remember, like so much of effective classroom management, it’s the little things that make the difference.
